## Welcome back

On April 23rd we discussed:

- uncertainty quantification (UQ)
- sensitivity analysis (SA)
- Sobol sensitivity indices
- Monte Carlo methods
- polynomial chaos expansions

Today we explore these ideas through interactive notebooks.

::: notes

The seminar in April focused on motivation, concepts, and applications.

Today's workshop is different.

Rather than introducing new theory, we will explore the ideas through notebooks and discussion.

The emphasis is on intuition and interpretation rather than derivations.

:::

## Today's approach

We begin hands-on with the G-star notebook.

The purpose is:

- not realism
- to build intuition and experience with UQSA

We focus on:

- first-order Sobol indices (importance)
- total-effect Sobol indices (interaction)

::: notes

Rather than starting with algorithms, we start with intuition.

The G-star notebook serves as a laboratory where we can directly observe how parameter importance and interactions influence model behaviour.

It will become our reference point for the rest of the workshop.

:::



## Colab workflow

Before modifying a notebook:

- File → Save a copy in Drive

General recommendations:

- modify parameters and sliders freely
- re-run cells when inputs change
- if something breaks, reload and continue from your saved copy

The notebooks are intended to be exploratory and robust.

::: notes

The most important practical step is saving your own copy before editing.

Then you can experiment freely without worrying about breaking anything.

:::



## Today's workshop

- G-star: building intuition for importance and interactions
-  uncertainty propagation with Monte Carlo
- polynomial chaos expansions
- comparison of methods
- discussion and wrap-up

::: notes

The order is deliberate.

We begin with a simple model that allows us to explore parameter
importance and interactions in an intuitive way.

We then move on to uncertainty propagation and polynomial chaos,
before comparing the different approaches and discussing
interpretation.

:::
